query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Using a machine learning potential (MLP) trained on ab initio molecular dynamics simulations can improve the representation of the liquid phase in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures
generation.intervention: Replacing EAM references with MLPs trained on ab initio molecular dynamics simulations
generation.conditions: High melting temperatures, multicomponent high-entropy alloys
generation.mechanism: Improved representation of the liquid phase through MLPs
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased reference-target phase-space overlap, reduced thermodynamic-integration path mismatch
generation.boundary: Applicable composition and temperature ranges: high-entropy alloys with 5 or more principal elements, temperatures near and above the melting point
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the generalizability of the MLPs to different alloy compositions and the potential for overfitting

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the free energies of melting predicted by the MLPs and EAM references for a set of high-entropy alloys
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the MLPs do not show a significant reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to the EAM references, the hypothesis is falsified
